title: No service owns each of the 14 data products, so the freshness stamp has no owner
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: Freshness
description: The freshness table names 14 products and their cycles but no source names the service that owns each product. RWB-E1-015 writes one data_product_load row per product per business date from v_ace_batch_status, which presumes a single owner for all 14, while D-RCV-60 gives each product's tables to the service that owns them.
evidence: Build Notes v6 'Freshness'; Arch v5 slide 15 (GET /freshness, AceDataReady and AceDataLate belong to rwb-source-data); Ownership Map v1 has no data product rows.
proposed: Name the owner of DP01 to DP14 in the PRDs and keep the stamp in P1 for Epic 1, or move a product's stamp to its owner and publish it on the owner's topic.

title: The per-service login names are not fixed in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: The grants
description: DP-02 and R4 require one login per service, but no source names the logins. The only login in the documents is the monolith login recovery_svc, which cannot serve 19 services.
evidence: Build Notes v6 'The grants'; Template and Rules R4 ('login per service') and DP-02.
proposed: Fix the login naming in the ACE DB stories of RWB-PLT-DB and state it in the Environment and Deployment Design next version.

title: The V0002 and V0003 grant block gives one monolith login, not one login per service
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-069 Read-only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule
description: The Grant note of RWB-E1-069 grants USAGE on recovery and SELECT on each view to recovery_svc, and DML on the 92 tables of schema recovery to the same role. D-RCV-60 replaces recovery_svc with one login per service (DP-02), so the grant block has to be rewritten per service even though the view list does not change.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-069 Grant note; Template and Rules DP-02 and ADR-014.
proposed: Split the V0002 and V0003 grant block into one grant per service login in RWB-PLT-DB, keeping ace_view_owner and the 30 views with P1.

title: The rule tables are described as recovery-schema tables but are owned by rwb-decision
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-072 Drools runtime and rule package store
description: The View note of RWB-E1-072 says the rule tables are in the recovery schema, and RWB-E1-073 stores the workbook, the generated DRL and the checksum there. The Ownership Map gives rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case to P7 rwb_decision, and the Temporal and Drools design puts governance centrally in rwb-decision with evaluation local in the owning service.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-072 and RWB-E1-073; Ownership Map v1 rule_package ruling (ASM-A6-tables-3); Temporal and Drools design slide 15.
proposed: Keep governance, the registry and the test cases in P7 and give each owning service only the evaluated copy (DP-04).

title: The retention tables are P1 tables in the story and P5 tables in the Ownership Map
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-017 Retention and archive rule for the data store
description: RWB-E1-017 owns retention_rule and retention_action and applies them to the 92 Workbench tables. The Ownership Map gives both tables to P5 rwb_document, which also applies retention to the document store.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-017; Ownership Map v1 retention_rule ruling (ASM-A6-tables-10).
proposed: Let P5 own both retention tables and the retention Schedule (JOB-17), and let P1 keep only a contract read.

title: The role table is loaded by P3 in the story and owned by P4 in the Ownership Map
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-019 Roles, teams and queues as data
description: RWB-E1-019 loads role, queue, queue_member, reference_row and reference_version as reference data. The Ownership Map gives role to P4 rwb_access and keeps queue, queue_member and the reference tables with P3.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-019; Ownership Map v1 role and queue rows; Template and Rules DP-07.
proposed: Load roles in P4 and read them in P3 by contract; keep teams, queues and the reference rows in P3.

title: The P2 outbound adapter writes a table owned by rwb-debtsale
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-007 Integration adapters for outbound files
description: RWB-E1-007 writes interface_config, outbound_item, outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event, debt_sale_account and recovery_case. Under D-RCV-60 debt_sale_account belongs to S6 rwb_debtsale and recovery_case to P3 rwb_case, so the adapter can no longer write them in its own transaction.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-007 View note; Ownership Map v1 debt_sale_account (S6) and recovery_case (P3).
proposed: Keep the file and outbox tables in P2, and let S6 own debt_sale_account with a contract call or an event from P2.

title: Feature flags are a P2 module table in the story and a platform library object in the Ownership Map
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-047 Feature flags for module release with a removal date
description: The section header places RWB-E1-047 in Module P2 Integration and the story owns feature_flag and feature_flag_change. The Ownership Map and the R-PREC default ruling give feature flags to the platform library, and the split plan gives the work to RWB-PLT-E1047.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-047; Ownership Map v1 feature_flag ruling (ASM-A6-tables-7); Template and Rules R3 default ruling.
proposed: Build the flag tables and the client in the platform library and let P2 serve the admin API against it.

title: The case story writes the P1 extension tables
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-018 Case ID issuance and case record v1
description: RWB-E1-018 writes recovery_case, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion, party_ext and account_ext. party_ext and account_ext are P1 extension tables in the Ownership Map, so a P3 story cannot write them in its own transaction.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-018 View note; Ownership Map v1 party_ext and account_ext (P1).
proposed: Keep the case tables in P3, write the extension rows in the P1 story RWB-P1-E1018-APP, and read them back by contract.

title: The Temporal platform and the Drools runtime sit in a P3 module in the story and in platform epics in the split plan
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-070, RWB-E1-071 and RWB-E1-072
description: The three configuration notes name Module P3 Case and workflow. The split plan gives their work to platform stories RWB-PLT-E1070, RWB-PLT-E1071 and RWB-PLT-E1072, in wave 0 lanes, and Arch v5 slides 45 and 16 describe one platform cluster and one shared kit for all 19 services.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-070 to RWB-E1-072; split plan legacy RWB-E1-070, RWB-E1-071 and RWB-E1-072; Arch v5 slide 45.
proposed: Keep the build order in the notes and read Module P3 as 'consumed by P3' rather than 'owned by P3'.

title: The run books are a P2 story in the notes and a platform OPS story in the split plan
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-056 Run books and monitoring for every Epic 1 Workbench job
description: The section header places RWB-E1-056 in Module P2 Integration, and the story reads job_catalog, data_product_load, case_list_row and reconciliation_result. The split plan gives the work to RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS in a platform lane, and the jobs it covers belong to nine different services.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-056; split plan legacy RWB-E1-056; Ownership Map v1 job_catalog ruling (ASM-A6-tables-9).
proposed: Publish the run book standard from the platform OPS story and let each service keep its own run book rows in its ops lane.

title: The data lake copy note remains in the build notes although the decision retires it
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-014 Decision log copy to the data lake
description: Arch v5 removes the data lake (DP-17), so RWB-E1-014 has no target and lake_copy_watermark is dropped. The note is still in the build notes and still describes a watermark and a copy step, which no Epic 1 story owns.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-014; Template and Rules R6 (Retired); Arch v5 slide 37; Ownership Map v1 lake_copy_watermark.
proposed: Keep the note as retired with no target and record the change in the Change Register, as R6 requires.

title: The Quartz note remains in the build notes although a Temporal Schedule replaces it
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-TE-007 Scheduled jobs on Quartz
description: D-RCV-60 retires RWB-TE-007 and points its dependencies to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, but the note still owns a Quartz schedule and job_catalog, and RWB-E1-030 still describes the JOB-06 chain behind it.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-TE-007 and RWB-E1-030; Template and Rules R6 (Retired) and DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44.
proposed: Read JOB-06 and every other Job in the map as a Temporal Schedule in the owning service and keep the retired note for traceability only.

title: The number of Epic 1 rule packages is not reconciled with the phase 1 package list
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-072 Drools runtime and rule package store
description: RWB-E1-072 seeds five Epic 1 package codes, while the Temporal and Drools design names eight phase 1 packages (ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT, TRANSFER, RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH). No source says which five are Epic 1.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-072 View note; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 phase 1 packages.
proposed: Name the five Epic 1 packages in the P7 story and let the remaining three arrive with their epics.

title: The sandbox story applies three migrations where 19 schemas now need their own sequence
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-065 Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data
description: RWB-E1-065 seeds the ACE schema, applies V0001 to V0003 and fills 88 Workbench tables and four extension tables. Under DP-15 each service has its own Flyway sequence in its own schema, so a three-migration sandbox cannot produce the 19 schemas the stories build on.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-065; Template and Rules DP-15 and ADR-021.
proposed: Build the sandbox from the 19 Flyway sequences plus the two view migrations and state the seeding order per schema.

title: The reconciliation story writes 'the case exceptions' without naming a table
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-E1-011 Reconciliation and data quality report
description: The View note of RWB-E1-011 writes reconciliation_result, case_list_row and 'the case exceptions'. No table of that name is in the Ownership Map, so the write cannot be assigned to a service.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-E1-011 View note; Ownership Map v1 table list.
proposed: Read 'the case exceptions' as the reconciliation breaks in reconciliation_result, or name the P3 case_entry_exclusion if that is meant.

title: The masked copy story writes the tables of three services from one platform story
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: RWB-TE-004 Masked data in SIT and UAT
description: RWB-TE-004 loads a masked copy of recovery_case, case_account, case_party, interaction, document_field, party_ext and contact_point_ext. Those tables belong to P3, P5 and P1, and the split plan gives the work to a platform story that owns no schema of its own.
evidence: Build Notes v6 RWB-TE-004; Ownership Map v1 table owners; split plan legacy RWB-TE-004.
proposed: Let the platform story supply the masking tool and each owning service load its own masked rows in its own story.

title: Service P8 takes Epic 1 stories in wave 1 although its Arch v5 wave is 2
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v6.md
section: Epic 1 and the 19 services
description: The W-MAP rule puts every EP01 story in wave 1, and the Service Story Catalog places the P8 Epic 1 stories in wave 1 lanes. Arch v5 slide 41 creates rwb-payment in wave 2. R5.6 keeps the earlier wave and raises one conflict row per service and business epic; the build notes have to say so, because the wave column of the story set no longer matches the service table.
evidence: Build Notes v6; Template and Rules R5.6 (W-MAP) and R4; Arch v5 slide 41; Service Story Catalog v1 Stories sheet.
proposed: State the wave 1 delivery of rwb-payment in the service epic and the wave plan, and let the rwb-payment service wave govern its later stories.
